purpose: Final post-family-freeze S4 selector-semantic residual closure batch, prioritized from the exact residual after selector batch 2.
policy: Only owner/source-supported selectors become executable. System-family entries reuse already-reviewed conservative per-owner/per-bridge singleton dependency namespaces; no historical EVM storage-layout or execution equivalence is claimed. Unknown selectors remain mapped-opaque. Exact coverage must be recomputed after application.

baseline.note: The pasted readiness report rounded coverage to two decimals; the checked-in batch therefore records observed marginal gains but does not manufacture an exact pre-apply numerator.

reviews.mapping_basis: Frozen traces place this state-capable selector on the already-reviewed zkSync Era DiamondProxy. Historical zkSync executor source and mainnet transaction/event evidence establish the block proof/verification lifecycle as a state transition. Reuse only the frozen per-chain singleton dependency lock; proof verification, batches, and storage layout are not reproduced.

Mainnet calls with this selector on the zkSync validator path emit BlockCommit events at the reviewed DiamondProxy, and zkSync source documents the block-commit lifecycle as state-mutating. Reuse the same conservative per-chain singleton dependency lock.

Frozen traces classify the selector as a successful state-capable call on the reviewed zkSync DiamondProxy; zkSync source documents executeBlocks-style finalization as a state transition. Preserve only the per-chain singleton dependency class.

Historical Arbitrum Bridge ABI/source identifies the observed delayed-message enqueue path as a bridge-global mutator. Reuse the frozen per-bridge singleton dependency abstraction rather than modeling bridge message arrays or accumulators directly.
The selector is a reviewed delayed-message count/read path. Model it as a read of the same per-bridge singleton dependency touched by delayed-message enqueue; no return-value equivalence is claimed.
Arbitrum Bridge ABI identifies sequencerMessageCount() as a read of bridge-global sequencer state. Model dependency only through the conservative per-bridge singleton read.

Arbitrum Bridge ABI identifies sequencerInboxAccs(uint256) as a read of bridge-global accumulator state. Preserve only the singleton dependency relationship; the index and return value are provenance, not native storage-layout claims.

Etherscan decodes 0x9f3ce55a on the exact Linea L1 Message Service as sendMessage(address,uint256,bytes); successful calls emit MessageSent/RollingHashUpdated and mutate messaging state. Reuse the reviewed Linea singleton lock dependency.

Verified BetIT source/ABI exposes enableTrading() together with buy/sell fee, max-transaction/max-wallet, swapping, and trading-policy state. Keep the already-frozen family classification unchanged and map only this owner+selector to a new conservative POLICY_MARKER singleton in the existing cw20-base native implementation. Standard CW20 selectors and other owners do not acquire this custom entrypoint; exact policy values and authorization are not reproduced.

XEN ABI binds 0x5bccb4c4 to claimMintRewardAndStake(uint256,uint256), an atomic mint-reward/stake mutation. The native XEN implementation now performs the corresponding user-mint removal, reward credit/stake creation, and global supply/stake updates atomically.
Etherscan decodes 0x7b0472f0 on the exact XEN token as stake(uint256,uint256). Reuse the existing native XEN balance/user-stake/global dependency implementation.
XEN ABI exposes withdraw() as the stake withdrawal path. Reuse the existing native XEN user-stake/balance/global state implementation.
0xa34123a7 is the canonical Uniswap V3 pool burn(int24,int24,uint128) mutator. Reuse the already-reviewed per-pool singleton dependency guard; no tick/liquidity math equivalence is claimed.
0x3c8a7d8d is the canonical Uniswap V3 pool mint(address,int24,int24,uint128,bytes) mutator. Reuse the reviewed per-pool singleton dependency guard only.

Standard transferFrom(address,address,uint256) on the reviewed legacy Synthetix implementation is state-mutating. Reuse only the existing per-owner singleton system dependency, consistent with the already-reviewed transfer path.

deferred.reason: OnBot custom selector identities remain unresolved. The family review only authorizes standard ERC20 dependency classes, so these remain opaque even though each has non-trivial residual gain.
Banana Gun selector semantics remain insufficiently supported for execution; keep opaque.
